samples.summary: Decrease-decimals no-op guard inspects raw value precision, not the decimals actually rendered, so it silently swallows a legitimate step
samples.evidence: `changeDecimals` returns early when `stepped < 0 && !explicitDp && await this.selectionRendersAt(0)` (sheet.ts:4198). `selectionRendersAt` (sheet.ts:4246-4261) only compares `decimalsInValue(cell.v)` — the raw stored string — and ignores any `dp`/`nf` the cell carries. Concrete case: A1 empty (no style anywhere → `explicitDp=false`, `dp=0`), B1 holds value `'12'` with cell style `{nf:'number', dp:3}` (renders `12.000`). Select A1:B1 with A1 active and press Decrease: `decimalsInValue('12') === 0` for B1, so the guard reports "nothing to drop" and returns without writing, even though B1 visibly shows three decimals and should step to two. The guard's own comment claims it exists precisely to catch "a neighbour that still shows decimals", but it measures the value, not what is shown.

samples.summary: Unsetting the last keys of a sheet/column/row style stores an empty `{}` layer instead of clearing it, so `resolveEffectiveStyle` stops returning undefined for those cells
samples.evidence: `omitStyleKeys` returns the stripped style even when it becomes `{}` (range-styles.ts:64-76). In the write phase the range-patch branch drops empties (`if (Object.keys(next).length > 0)`, sheet.ts:4481), but the sheet/column/row branches do not: `this.colStyles.set(col, next); await this.store.setColumnStyle(col, next)` (sheet.ts:4451-4452), same for rows (4464-4465) and sheet style (4439-4440). A column whose style was exactly `{dp:1, nf:'number'}` therefore keeps an empty entry in `colStyles`/the store. `resolveEffectiveStyle` short-circuits to `undefined` only when every layer is falsy (sheet.ts:883), so afterwards `getStyle` on every cell of that column returns `{}` rather than `undefined` — the new tests themselves work around this by asserting `style?.dp` instead of `style` for the column/row/all round trips (test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:326-360) while the cell-level tests assert `toBeUndefined()`. The empty layer is also persisted/synced forever.

samples.summary: Decrease at the zero floor still writes a style patch, and can add `nf:'number'` to a cell that only had an explicit `dp`
samples.evidence: When `explicitDp` is true the early-return guard is skipped, so `stepped < 0` falls through to `clamped=true, target=0` and always calls `setRangeStyle({dp: 0, ...})` (sheet.ts:4208-4235). Two consequences: (a) every extra Decrease press at the floor appends another range-style patch / store write (and undo step) that changes nothing; (b) the `if (!nf || nf === 'plain') patch.nf = 'number'` branch fires for a cell that stored `dp` without any `nf`, so a clamped Decrease *adds* a number format (and its grouping separators) although the comment at 4205-4207 states "the stored format stays put instead of being unset along the way".

samples.summary: `decimalsInValue` counts every character after the first dot, so exponent/text values yield nonsense precision that is then written as `dp`
samples.evidence: `return dotIndex >= 0 ? value.length - dotIndex - 1 : 0` (format.ts:97). For a formula result in exponential form such as `'1.2345678901234567e+21'` it returns 20, and for text like `'a.bcd'` it returns 3. `getActiveDecimalState` feeds that straight into `dp` for plain-format cells (sheet.ts:4183) and `changeDecimals` then writes `{dp: valueDp + 1}` (sheet.ts:4231), i.e. `maximumFractionDigits` values above 20 reaching `toLocaleString` in `formatValue` (format.ts:127-130); `safeFormat`'s catch retries with the *same* options (format.ts:14-18), so on any engine that rejects >20 fraction digits the RangeError escapes uncaught. It also makes the round-trip logic (`target === valueDp`) meaningless for text cells.

samples.summary: Cell scan normalizes to merge anchors, so a partially selected merged cell can have its style keys stripped even though the anchor lies outside the selection
samples.evidence: `const anchor = this.normalizeRefToAnchor(parseRef(sref))` (sheet.ts:4407) maps any covered cell to its merge anchor, and the anchor's style (which governs the whole merged region, possibly extending outside the selection) is then rewritten by `omitStyleKeys` at 4425. Unlike the col/row/sheet layers there is no ownership check for the cell layer, so a selection covering only part of a merge can strip `dp`/`nf` from cells it does not cover. Multi-range selections (`this.ranges`) are not expanded to merged boundaries by `selectionTargets` (4308-4312), unlike `getRangeOrActiveCell`.

samples.summary: Read-modify-write over an await boundary: cells are snapshotted in the scan phase and re-written later from the stale snapshot
samples.evidence: The scan phase stores `existing` (sheet.ts:4414) in `cellEdits`, and the write phase later does `compactCell(cell, nextStyle)` from that snapshot (sheet.ts:4491-4497) after many intervening `await`s (further `store.get`s, `setSheetStyle`, `setColumnStyle`, `setRangeStyles`). Any concurrent local or remote mutation of a cell's `v`/`f` in that window is clobbered by the stale snapshot.

finding.summary: Decrease-decimals no-op guard inspects raw value precision, not the decimals actually rendered, so it silently swallows a legitimate step
finding.evidence: `changeDecimals` returns early when `stepped < 0 && !explicitDp && await this.selectionRendersAt(0)` (sheet.ts:4198). `selectionRendersAt` (sheet.ts:4246-4261) only compares `decimalsInValue(cell.v)` — the raw stored string — and ignores any `dp`/`nf` the cell carries. Concrete case: A1 empty (no style anywhere → `explicitDp=false`, `dp=0`), B1 holds value `'12'` with cell style `{nf:'number', dp:3}` (renders `12.000`). Select A1:B1 with A1 active and press Decrease: `decimalsInValue('12') === 0` for B1, so the guard reports "nothing to drop" and returns without writing, even though B1 visibly shows three decimals and should step to two. The guard's own comment claims it exists precisely to catch "a neighbour that still shows decimals", but it measures the value, not what is shown.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. changeDecimals returns early at sheet.ts:4198 when `stepped < 0 && !explicitDp && await this.selectionRendersAt(0)`, and selectionRendersAt (sheet.ts:4246-4261) inspects only `cell.v` via decimalsInValue (format.ts:92-98), a pure string scan of the raw stored value; it never reads the cell's `dp`/`nf`. Since formatValue renders with `dp ?? 2` under `nf:'number'` (format.ts:119-131), a cell storing '12' with {nf:'number', dp:3} visibly shows 12.000 yet reports 0 decimals to the guard. With an empty unstyled active cell (getActiveDecimalState returns dp:0, explicitDp:false at sheet.ts:4182-4184), a Decrease over such a selection returns without writing, so the styled neighbour never steps down. This contradicts both the guard's own comment (sheet.ts:4201-4202) and the design doc (docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:269-271, 'if another selected cell still shows decimals, the step is written after all'). The path is user-reachable via Spreadsheet's decrease handler (spreadsheet.ts:546), and existing tests only cover the raw-value variant (decimals.test.ts:145-158), so nothing guards or refutes it. Real logic bug (wrong condition / silently swallowed action) in the correctness lane.

mergedFrom.summary: Round-trip unset of `dp` on currency/percent formats *increases* the displayed decimals, because an absent `dp` means the format's default (2), not the value's own precision

finding.summary: Increase/decrease decimals silently deletes a user-chosen `nf: 'number'` format (and its thousands grouping) whenever the stepped dp happens to equal the value's own precision
finding.evidence: When `nf === 'number'` the unset request is `{ dp, nf }` (sheet.ts:4219-4220), i.e. the number format itself is removed. The code cannot distinguish an `nf:'number'` the user chose from one a previous step added. Example: A1 = `1234.5` with `{nf:'number', dp:0}` (grouped, no decimals — a state a user reaches with the toolbar or that the importer writes). Click *increase* decimals: dp=0, valueDp=1, target=1===valueDp, selectionRendersAt(1) true → `unsetRangeStyleValues({dp:0, nf:'number'})` strips both keys → display goes from `1,234` to `1234.5`, i.e. the grouping/number format the user chose is destroyed by an increase-decimals click. The existing test 'should keep a number format the user chose' only covers the case where valueDp differs from the target, so this path is untested.

verdict.reason: The finding describes the unset path as gated by `selectionRendersAt(target)`, which is not what the code does. `changeDecimals` gates the `{dp, nf}` unset on `await this.unsetKeepsRendering(nf, target)` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4211-4229). `unsetKeepsRendering` (sheet.ts:4275-4300) compares, for every non-empty cell in the selection, `formatValue(value, nfAfter=undefined, undefined)` against `formatValue(value, nf, target)` and returns false on any difference. `formatValue` returns the raw string for an absent/plain format (format.ts:111-113) and uses Intl grouping for `'number'` (format.ts:124-131), so the reviewer's exact example (`1234.5` with `{nf:'number', dp:0}`, increase → target 1) compares `'1234.5'` vs `'1,234.5'`, differs, `unsetKeepsRendering` returns false, and the code falls through to the explicit `setRangeStyle({dp: 1})` write keeping `nf:'number'`. So display never goes from `1,234` to `1234.5` and the grouping/number format is not destroyed. Contrary to the claim that "this path is untested", the scenario is covered verbatim by `should keep a grouped number format the user chose` (packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:114-127, value `1234.5`, style `{dp:0, nf:'number'}`, increase → expects `{dp:1, nf:'number'}`) and by decimals.test.ts:94-112. The only remaining case where the unset does drop `nf:'number'` is one where every selected cell renders byte-identically afterwards (e.g. `1.5`), which is the documented intent of the reversibility rule, not the grouping/format loss alleged.

finding.summary: Decrease decimals becomes a silent no-op for a multi-cell selection whenever the active cell has no explicit dp, even though other selected cells have decimals to drop
finding.evidence: `if (stepped < 0 && !explicitDp) { return; }` (sheet.ts:4198-4202) is decided purely from the ACTIVE cell. Select A1:B1 where A1=`12` (no style → dp=0, explicitDp=false) and B1=`1.2345` (no style). Clicking decrease decimals now returns before touching anything, so B1 keeps 4 decimals. The previous implementation (spreadsheet.ts, removed lines) wrote `{dp: Math.max(0, dp-1), nf:'number'}` over the whole selection, so B1 went to 0 decimals. The new test 'should keep stepping a selection whose active cell is already at zero' only exercises the case where the active cell has an *explicit* dp:0 (the `clamped` branch), so this regression is uncovered.

verdict.reason: The finding quotes the guard as `if (stepped < 0 && !explicitDp) { return; }`, decided purely from the active cell. The actual code at sheet.ts:4198 is `if (stepped < 0 && !explicitDp && (await this.selectionRendersAt(0)))` — a third conjunct that inspects the whole selection. `selectionRendersAt` (sheet.ts:4246-4261) walks every range returned by `selectionTargets()` (sheet.ts:4308-4312, which returns the full `this.ranges` when a range is selected) and returns false as soon as any numeric cell's `decimalsInValue` differs from the target. In the claimed repro (A1=`12`, B1=`1.2345`), `decimalsInValue('1.2345')` = 4 (format.ts:92-98) != 0, so `selectionRendersAt(0)` is false, the early return does not fire, and control falls through to `clamped = true` / `target = 0` and the `setRangeStyle({dp: 0, nf: 'number'})` write at sheet.ts:4231-4235 — the same whole-selection behavior the finding claims was regressed. The no-op only occurs when every numeric cell in the selection already renders at 0 decimals, i.e. when there is genuinely nothing to drop. The described code is not present as characterized.

finding.summary: Comment/assumption that dropping `nf:'number'` keeps the cell looking the same is false — grouping separators are lost
finding.evidence: Lines 4204-4207 justify removing `nf` with "the cell keeps looking the same", but `formatValue(value,'number',dp)` goes through `toLocaleString` (format.ts:127-130) which adds thousands separators, while plain format returns the raw string verbatim (format.ts:111-113). For value '1234.5': with {nf:'number',dp:1} the cell shows '1,234.5'; after the unset it shows '1234.5'. The new test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:89-92 encodes exactly this lossy outcome (`toBe('1234.5')`). So decrease-then-increase on a number-formatted cell silently drops the user's number format and its grouping.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. sheet.ts:4205-4207 is a comment about the negative-step clamp, not a claim that dropping `nf` keeps the cell looking the same. The nf-dropping unset at sheet.ts:4224-4228 is gated by `await this.unsetKeepsRendering(nf, target)` (sheet.ts:4215), which at sheet.ts:4281-4298 sets `nfAfter = nf === 'number' ? undefined : nf` and refuses whenever `formatValue(value, nfAfter, undefined, options)` differs from `formatValue(value, nf, target, options)` for any cell in the selection. For '1234.5' the plain branch returns the verbatim string (format.ts:111-113) while the 'number' branch returns toLocaleString's '1,234.5' (format.ts:124-131), so they differ and the unset is refused, falling through to the explicit write at sheet.ts:4231-4235 — exactly the grouping-preservation the finding claims is absent (and the doc comment at sheet.ts:4267-4273 names that scenario). The cited test is also misquoted: decimals.test.ts:78-92 uses '12.5' (line 80) and asserts toBe('12.5') at line 91 — an ungrouped value where the unset is genuinely lossless — not toBe('1234.5'). The '1234.5' case is covered separately at decimals.test.ts:94-112, which asserts the style stays {dp:1, nf:'number'} and the display equals the grouped formatValue('1234.5','number',1). Display uses the same formatValue path (sheet.ts:962-970), so the guard's comparison matches what the user sees.
